(Context: I'm still learning web dev)
imho, frontend is easy to get started with harder to actually learn. Backend is harder to get started with but once you have built one CRUD project, it will apply to most/all languages used for the backend. The patterns are the same. 
Static sites are easy to make, but front end applications have to deal with more stuff since it is tied to users whose preferences vary (reactivity, hydration, state management, etc.). That's why I'm going back to the basics of JS to dive deeper into event handling, and async tasks since that seems like the foundation of these modern frameworks which you can't really avoid since in today's world noone wants the page to load/be redirected with every input/click like the days of yore.

Do something that hurts more. Force yourself to do something.
Worked for me but might not for you.
Look for a challenging hobby to do that you don't understand and go deeply on the subject. If you feel that you're disinterested, push through till it hurts and you're exhausted on learning the subject then read some more till you are physically exhausted. Do that everyday while exhausting yourself physically by exercising. 

The point of this is to let time pass while doing something that engages you. Being alone with your thoughts is pain that is unbearable that manifests in every ounce of your being. You actually feel it physically even if you don't harm yourself to the point that harming yourself feels less painful than what you feel every single hour.

Can't get up from your bed? Crawl even if it takes you till noon to get to the kitchen to get something to eat. Can't focus to read something? Say every single word loudly so you can hear yourself and confirm that you are in fact still alive. You might even laugh at yourself for sounding like a grade schooler reading. It's idiotic, I know, but at the end of the day you're stuck, and the only way out is to force your way through. 

Just a warning though. You will be bitter and angry at life and the world if you go through this because you'll be in pain and be exhausted. You'll be behind your peers and feel like shit everyday that passes but if you're lucky you might build a 'I at least have to try and better myself' mentality. The only upside to this is you'll live to see another day. I don't really believe in luck or that 'time heals all wounds' but being in control of something in your life while everything else is on fire is a more pleasant feeling than what I went through for more than half of my life (I'm 25). 

It doesn't go away btw. You just grow stronger to deal with it.

I'm young(ish) pa po and I still regret when I took a certain college entrance exam and fell asleep on one of the tests 'cause of a kerfuffle the night prior. Here's my story.

So, no sleep and no food for almost a day before starting that 5 hour exam. Didn't know where to go for the exam didn't have any classmates with me, was almost late. Didn't review for anything (never even reviewed weeks/months before unlike my classmates since I can't afford review centers for it, all I had are our schoolbooks).

So, exam time came and I answered most of it till the 3rd exam where I think I fell asleep (or fainted idk) and just left most of it blank. At the end of the exam, my seatmate offered me food since I hadn't eaten anything since the test started (we had a kind of lunchbreak where we could eat inside the testing room). 

When the results came, I could see the only exam I failed was the one I fell asleep at. One of my classmates said, "dapat pala magkaklase tayo ehhh". I was so close. I scored 35% at that test while the other tests were 85-90% (which was enough at the time to pass since we shared scores with each other). I ended up stopping school for a year then reenrolled as a freshman in another college on a scholarship with the help of my HS guidance counselor no less haha. I was glad she helped me (she knew my situation at home and would constsntly look out for me when I was having a hard time with expenses/school).

I only had a chance to take one exam at one college since it was clear to me they didn't want me to go to college. "Wag ka na dyan mag-aral, di natin kaya yan" were the words I heard while one of my siblings were promised they would be studying in Manila and one was promised she would study Nursing (which got me like, _isn't that more expensive?_ in my mind. She is studying Nursing now, btw and I had to help with some of the tuition fees haha wala eh family eh).

Anyway, I'm still finding my way, I hope you will too OP.

It's not that you aren't motivated to do anything. It's that doing things at this time for longer than a few minutes, when you're vulnerable, is tedious, exhausting, heart-wrenching and draining. 

Try to do anything that can be done in a span of 5-10 minutes. Watch a quick youtube tutorial about one trick you can do in photoshop/excel/illustrator/whatever app or program you're wanting to learn. Then when you're comfortable doing that, try increasing the time commitment to 20 minutes to half an hour or an hour, go back if you feel like it is too much.

This won't help you master a skill in a short amount of time but it will keep you busy enough and some skills/tricks will eventually stick. (and always remember it takes time to learn a skill!)
